key_insight: Putting trainable nonlinear functions on physical connections, rather than using devices only as scalar weights, makes analogue neural networks much more effective for smooth continuous-control and regression tasks.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a path to ultra-low-power edge AI hardware for robotics, control, and solar maximum-power-point tracking, with a projected CMOS power of about 30 microwatts.
method: Implemented connection-wise nonlinear functions as analogue band-pass filters on field-programmable analogue arrays.
Trained physical networks inspired by Kolmogorov-Arnold networks so each connection becomes a learnable computational element.
Compared performance across continuous targets and decision-boundary-like tasks, and validated transfer to hardware and memristive simulation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantified hardware transfer across roughly 35,000 connections and shows the approach uses far fewer nodes and connections than multilayer perceptrons on smooth continuous targets.
watch_item: The benefit is task-dependent and does not provide a parameter-efficiency advantage for classification-like decision boundaries, so it is not a universal replacement for standard networks.
paper_title: Low-power analogue neural networks with trainable nonlinear connections for continuous control
